extracted.intended_audience: EPA decisionmakers, agency rule writers, agency counsel, and public-interest commenters evaluating agency use of scientific information
extracted.subtask_description: A notice-and-comment legal submission challenging EPA’s reliance on the Draft CWG Report by evaluating that Report and agency conduct against federal scientific-integrity and information-quality standards. Focuses on peer review, transparency, objectivity, and procedural requirements (FACA/OMB/DOE/EPA/OSTP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 14303: nine scientific integrity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered compliant with the Administration’s policies, research must be (1) reproducible; (2) transparent; (3) communicative of error and uncertainty; (4) collaborative and interdisciplinary; (5) skeptical of its findings and assumptions; (6) structured for falsifiability of hypotheses; (7) subject to unbiased peer review; (8) accepting of negative results as positive outcomes; and (9) without conflicts of interest. (Exec. Order No. 14303, § 3.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSTP was directed to issue implementation guidance and agencies to adopt scientific integrity policies that implement these nine principles. The comment finds the Draft CWG Report adheres to none of these principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: OSTP guidance on peer review and review practices
rubrics_metrics.description: OSTP guidance directs agencies to ensure peer review that is 'impartial and independent' prior to publication or dissemination and explains that 'effective unbiased peer review relies on transparent, well-defined review criteria, competent and independent reviewers, and robust mechanisms to minimize conflicts of interest, often facilitated by double-blind or open peer review by qualified experts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSTP directs agencies to ensure appropriate reviewer selection prioritizing expertise, independence, and viewpoint diversity, adopt double-blind review where appropriate, and require clear disclosure of potential conflicts of interest. The Draft CWG Report purportedly failed to meet these OSTP expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Information Quality Bulletin for Peer Review: peer review requirements and tiers
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB’s 2005 Bulletin requires that 'important scientific information shall be peer reviewed by qualified specialists before it is disseminated by the Federal government' and establishes tiers (including influential scientific information (ISI) and highly influential scientific assessments (HISA)) subject to different degrees of peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For HISA, peer review is more rigorous and reviewers should be provided access to underlying data or models; peer review should, 'wherever possible, provide for public participation'; and agencies must 'disseminate the peer review report and the agency’s response to the report on the agency’s Web site.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and thresholds for HISA/Influential Scientific Information (OMB)
rubrics_metrics.description: An HISA is an assessment where 'the agency or the OIRA Administrator determines that the dissemination could have a potential impact of more than $500 million in any one year on either the public or private sector or that the dissemination is novel, controversial, or precedent-setting, or has significant interagency interest.' (70 Fed. Reg. at 2671.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HISA status triggers heightened peer review requirements including access to data/models and public participation; agencies should make peer review reports available in time for public consideration if the information supports a final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE/agency-specific influential-information threshold (DOE definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE’s definition of 'influential information' includes 'information on which a regulatory action with a $100 million per year impact is based.' (DOE IQA Guidelines.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comment notes DOE/EPA reliance on the Draft CWG Report (cited 22 times) and the regulatory consequences (potentially repealing vehicle GHG regulations), supporting the argument that the Report is 'influential' or HISA and thus subject to heightened review standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE Information Quality Act (IQA) Guidelines: quality, objectivity, utility, integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE must 'maximize the quality, objectivity, utility, and integrity of information (including statistical information) disseminated to the public.' DOE IQA Guidelines outline expectations that scientific information be accurate, reliable, unbiased, and comply with OMB Bulletin requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidelines require evaluation of clarity of hypotheses, validity of research design, quality of data collection procedures, robustness of methods, appropriateness of methods for hypotheses, extent to which conclusions follow from analysis, and strengths and limitations of the product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present information 'accurate, clear, complete and unbiased' with sound methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency guidance states disseminated information should be 'presented in an accurate, clear, complete and unbiased manner' and, in a scientific context, 'the original and supporting data should be generated, and the analytical results developed, using sound statistical and research methods.' (DOE IQA Guidelines at 12, 17.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If work has been subjected to formal, independent, external peer review it 'may generally be presumed to be of acceptable objectivity.' The comment argues the Draft CWG Report fails these substance and methodological standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and disclosure requirements (including FACA records disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: When transparency is relevant to information usefulness, DOE Elements should ensure transparency is addressed; FACA requires disclosure of committee records. Agencies must disclose materials made available to and prepared by advisory committees and ensure public access to records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comment asserts DOE/CWG failed to disclose materials, hindering public assessment and diminishing quality/utility under DOE IQA and FACA; secrecy in committee formation and operations violates these transparency requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA Peer Review Policy and Handbook expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA guidance states that 'for highly influential scientific assessments, external peer review is the expected procedure. For influential scientific information intended to support important decisions...external peer review is the approach of choice.' (EPA Peer Review Policy/Memo; Peer Review Handbook.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA maintains procedural guidance (Peer Review Handbook 4th ed.) and Scientific Integrity Policy; the comment argues DOE and EPA did not follow these EPA peer review expectations in relation to the Draft CWG Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review procedural elements: reviewer independence, diversity, and conflict-minimization
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB/OSTP/EPA guidance requires 'a broad and diverse representation of respected perspectives and intellectual traditions within the scientific community,' reviewers independent of the sponsoring agency, prioritizing expertise, independence, and viewpoint diversity, and robust mechanisms to minimize conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance suggests double-blind or open peer review where appropriate and clear disclosure of potential conflicts. The comment highlights that CWG membership and review lacked independence, viewpoint diversity, and conflict controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological transparency and documentation of study selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific assessments should disclose methodological procedures, including how studies, models, and data were chosen; provide criteria for selecting resources; and document underlying data and assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSTP guidance and scientific norms require quantification of statistical uncertainties and clear criteria enabling falsifiability and testing. The comment criticizes the Draft CWG Report for failing to quantify uncertainties, using vague language ('possibly detrimental to', 'might be underestimated') and analyzing only a small fraction of literature compared to IPCC/NCA practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of calibrated confidence/likelihood language
rubrics_metrics.description: Leading scientific assessments (e.g., IPCC) use calibrated language to express levels of confidence and likelihood (very high, high, medium, low, etc., with associated probability ranges) to communicate uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSTP guidance directs quantifying uncertainties; the comment contrasts IPCC calibrated language with the Draft CWG Report’s broad narrative claims and lack of quantified uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to underlying data and models for HISA peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review for highly influential scientific assessments should provide reviewers access to underlying data or models so the review can examine the basis for conclusions. (OMB Bulletin, 70 Fed. Reg. at 2671.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HISA peer review expectations also include public participation where possible and publishing peer review reports. The comment notes DOE/CWG did not provide such access or disclose the internal review participants and feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to publish peer review report and agency response prior to/during rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to 'disseminate the peer review report and the agency’s response to the report on the agency’s Web site' and, if the scientific information is used to support a final rule, the peer review report should be made available 'with enough time for the public to consider the implications of the peer review report for the rule being considered.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comment argues DOE/EPA did not meet these dissemination and transparency obligations for the Draft CWG Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-dissemination external peer review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: OSTP and OMB guidance direct that impartial and independent peer review occur 'prior to...publication[] or dissemination' of important scientific information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Draft CWG Report was 'disseminated by the Department of Energy' and thus, under DOE/OMB guidance, required external peer review before dissemination; the comment alleges only internal undisclosed review occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation in peer review where practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB and DOE guidance state that peer review processes should, wherever possible, provide for public participation in the review of influential scientific information and HISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comment notes the absence of public participation opportunities and urges EPA to review comments submitted to DOE in addition to those in the EPA docket given uncertainty about CWG comment handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation factors for quality of scientific/technical information (EPA Science Policy Council factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA Science Policy Council materials outline general assessment factors for evaluating the quality of scientific and technical information (e.g., relevance, objectivity, reliability, transparency, reproducibility, and completeness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comment references these EPA assessment factors and asserts the Draft CWG Report violates them by being inaccurate, biased, reliant on unreputable sources, and lacking transparency and appropriate peer review.
